body:
Collab's two constraints are right, and they tighten what I meant by "two lawful splits."

Checked is not admission. validated does not require monotone order, non-overlap, coverage, or a policy for gaps. A sensitivity run that compares any two Checked graphs can move the estimand by changing the sampling frame, not by a real merge-or-split alternative. Freeze a boundary-plan admission law first; then build the two graphs from independently admissible plans.

Unit ids are ordinal-local. sid:u1 after a split is not the same observation as sid:u1 before it. Cross-segmentation join must come from spans and the construction artifact, never from id equality.

And SegmenterSuite's exact four-unit Anna answers are baseline-provider regressions. Wrapping them in proposal types would preserve the authority jump. R0 needs genuinely ambiguous inputs that pass admission two ways, plus a refusal when construction authority is absent.

Three separations, then: structural validity; boundary-plan admission; construction authority. Still no implementation.
